x: These two youngsters should be a great help to our teams for many seasons to come, and to beat such experienced runners as Tom Carter, Albert Frost and Bert Mitchell was a really grand performance.

George Chantler finished 6th but was running for our "B" team who were placed 4th while our "C" team finished 6th out of an entry of nine teams. On the 17th April in the Walton 10 miles race, Tom Clinton finished first with Tom Carter fifth, Geoff Pearson 14th and Bert Mitchell 16th.

Thirty runners, comprising seven teams finished the course and although our numbers were small, our lads all ran very well and we are sorry to hear that Bert Mitchell has been advised to give up distance running owing to leg trouble.

Frank Abberton, last year's winner, retired after 10 miles and Bert Mitchell also dropped out owing to leg trouble. Actual times and positions of our men were as follows: 13, Footer, 2 hrs. 55 mins. 46 secs.; 17, Ring, 2.58.48; 22, Smith, 3.3.4; 28, Chantler, 3.5.11; 39, Pearson, 3.10.40; 40, Porter…
Thanks are due to Bert Mitchell for kindly presenting two miniature shields for this year's Marathon Championship. Doug Whitehead writes from Abusultan, M.E.A.F., that he has gained his R.A.F.
When they came in sight of the finish our old friend Bert Mitchell was in the lead followed by young Dick Savage, with a new youngster in E.

I have not yet come across a 120 yards hurdles time—junior or senior—worthy of being accounted a Club record, and I should be glad to hear of a good hurdles performance. Bert Mitchell's Marathon time was over the measured Blackpool Corporation course. He finished 2nd, running for Ford Motors S.C.

And ALBERT WATTAM in Lincolnshire, TOMMY GREEN (our 1932 Olympic Champion) in Hampshire, STAN VICKERS, the CHURCHERS, DON BROWN at Richmond, JOE FLOWER and BERT MITCHELL in Kent ? - And the many others who have added something to the Belgrave story in the years that are passed ?

BERT MITCHELL, always associated with our Club Marathon Championship Shield, paid us a visit on the occasion of the 20 Miles Open Run and promises that his next visit to Wimbledon will not be so long delayed.

The "Mitchell Trophy"is being awarded by the donor of this magnificent shield, Bert Mitchell of 32, Manor Road, Deal. Bert was formerly a fierce competitor and still remains a staunch Belgrave Harrier.
In addition to the letters read out, a number of members had let us know that they could not attend. Bert Mitchell, one of our earliest marathon runners who now lives in Deal.
